audit.whatIsWrong: The page's core claim is that Tangle-Barbs locks Kassadin out of Riftwalk — 'if she lands E root into the airborne Pop Blossom stun, all your mobility means nothing', 'eating the E means you eat the whole chain', 'blink the instant her E flies'. Riftwalk is a blink and roots do not disable blinks.
audit.why: Pre-6 the conclusion is right for the wrong reason: he has no escape because he has no ultimate. From 6 the reason stops holding, and the page never updates — a rooted Kassadin can still Riftwalk out in the window between the root landing and Pop Blossom's leap. What genuinely locks the blink is the knock-up itself, which is a different ability on a 120-second cooldown.
audit.corrected: Split apart in spikes[1].text, spikes[2].text, whys[4], phases[4].why, content.mid, content.late, breakdown.mid, tradeGood, dontsFull[1] and Key Ability Interactions.

audit.whatIsWrong: Inherent Glamour hides Pop Blossom's preparation while Neeko is disguised. Riot's text says so explicitly and neither layer mentions it.
audit.why: It is the reason this matchup produces deaths that feel unfair. The page repeatedly tells the player to 'sidestep her R wind-up' — there is no wind-up to see if she is wearing an ally's model. The counterplay is not reaction, it is refusing to stand next to unexplained allies.
audit.corrected: Written into enemyWin, breakdown.cooldowns and Key Ability Interactions, and the 'sidestep the wind-up' advice in content.mid corrected.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tangle-Barbs grows: Riot's text says if it kills an enemy or passes through a champion it becomes larger, faster, and roots for longer. Nothing on the page says so.
audit.why: It converts 'sidestep the root' into something a player can actually act on — the root that kills you is the one that ate a dying caster minion on the way. Standing behind a low-health wave is the single most common way this lane loses a Kassadin.
audit.corrected: Stated in tradeBad, wants.foe[0], dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns and content.early.

audit.whatIsWrong: full.diff reads FAV and diffRating 5.5/10 with both rating lines saying 'Even matchup', while every phase in the chart is sided Neeko — six of seven, several at 2/10 — and the packet records 33.33% for Kassadin.
audit.why: The verdict fields say favoured, the chart says he loses almost every stage, and the win rate agrees with the chart. FAV is three characters and cannot be changed inside the band, but the numbers around it can at least stop contradicting it.
audit.corrected: diffRating 5.5/10 to 7.5/10 and both rating lines reworded to 'Hard matchup'. See notes on the sample size.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0] to [5] are the generic Kassadin boilerplate and phases[4] promises that at 6 'short blink-trades start working' on a row the chart sides Neeko at 2/10.
audit.why: The level-6 row is the one place the two layers could agree — content.mid says explicitly 'Do NOT use it to engage' — and the full layer tells the player the opposite on the same stage.
audit.corrected: phases[0], [2], [3], [4] and [5] rewritten; level 6 now describes the blink as an escape from the root, not an engage.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns gives no numbers — 'sidestep it behind minions', 'it governs your forward steps'.
audit.why: Tangle-Barbs is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s and Pop Blossom is 120/105/90s. The gap between those two is the whole plan: her root comes back every twelve seconds and her lockdown every two minutes, so only one of them is worth waiting out.
audit.corrected: Both written into breakdown.cooldowns, phases[3].why, dosFull[2].d, tradeGood and All-In Windows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Void Stone appears as '15% magic reduction' in wants.you[1] and content.late; phases[2].why carries the 'E only charges when spells fly' boilerplate; breakdown.late says 'Q-silence the counterplay'.
audit.why: Void Stone has been 10% since V11.24; Force Pulse stopped being charge-gated in V12.23 and is now a 21/20/19/18/17s cooldown shortened by a second per nearby cast; Null Sphere has no silence.
audit.corrected: 15% set to 10% in both places, phases[2].why moved to the cooldown model, silence replaced with the shield.

edits.before: Neeko owns these levels and you simply accept it. Her Q (Blooming Burst) bounces off your caster minions for free poke, and her W (Shapesplitter) lets her disguise as a minion or ally so you often can't tell where the real Neeko is standing. You have only Null Sphere and no mana sustain yet, so do not trade — last-hit at max range, eat the chip, and save your Q shield to soak a poke instance rather than start a fight. The thing that ends you here is her E (Tangle-Barbs): if she roots you at level 2-3 you have no Riftwalk to blink out, and you die before the fight starts.
edits.after: Neeko owns these levels and you simply accept it. Blooming Burst bounces off your caster minions for free poke, and Shapesplitter lets her wear a minion or an ally so you often can't tell where the real Neeko stands. You have only Null Sphere and no mana sustain, so do not trade — last-hit at max range, eat the chip, and save the Q shield to soak a poke instance rather than start a fight. What ends you is Tangle-Barbs: it grows if it kills a minion on the way, so never stand behind a dying caster, and at 2-3 you have no Riftwalk to leave the root.

edits.before: Nether Blade's mana restore and a maxed Null Sphere finally let you farm under tower without going hollow, but you are still behind through 4-5 — this is weather-the-storm, not a fight window. Level 6 is your one breath: Riftwalk lets you blink the moment her E flies or sidestep her R wind-up, dodge her roams, and escape a gank that would otherwise be free. Do NOT use it to engage — she out-ranges you and the Pop Blossom airborne stun lands if you blink into it. Blink to safety, farm, and survive.
edits.after: Nether Blade's mana restore and a maxed Null Sphere finally let you farm under tower without going hollow, but you are still behind through 4-5 — weather-the-storm, not a fight window. Level 6 is your one breath: roots do not stop blinks, so Riftwalk leaves Tangle-Barbs before the follow-up lands, and it escapes the gank that would otherwise be free. Do NOT use it to engage. And do not expect to see her R start — while she is disguised, Pop Blossom's preparation is hidden.

edits.before: This is the whole reason you suffered the lane. With Rod of Ages online and Riftwalk stacking its escalating damage, your blink-spam lets you flank onto Neeko's squishy frame and burst her before Shapesplitter can disguise her and slip away. Void Stone's 15% magic reduction plus an early Null Magic Mantle / MR item makes her Pop Blossom and Q burst far less lethal, and your Null Sphere shield eats the opener. The catch: never get chain-CC'd. If she lands E (Tangle-Barbs) root into the airborne Pop Blossom stun, all your mobility means nothing — track her R cooldown and only commit when it is down.
edits.after: This is the whole reason you suffered the lane. With Rod of Ages online and Riftwalk stacking its escalating damage, your blink-spam lets you flank onto Neeko's squishy frame and burst her before Shapesplitter can disguise her and slip away. The catch is the knock-up, not the root: you can blink out of Tangle-Barbs, but not out of a Pop Blossom already on top of you. Track its 90-second clock.

notes: SAMPLE CAVEAT ON THE RATING CHANGE: this matchup has 6 recorded games at 33.33%. That is far too thin to grade a lane on by itself, and I would not have moved diffRating on the win rate alone. I moved it because the page contradicts itself independently of the sample — full.diff says FAV while all seven phase rows are sided Neeko, four of them at 2/10. The new 7.5/10 agrees with the chart the page already publishes. If the chart is what is wrong, then diffRating should go back to 5.5 and the chart should be rebuilt instead; someone with more games should decide which. full.diff itself is three characters ('FAV') and no correct value fits the 10% band, so it still reads FAV and still contradicts everything around it. THE DISGUISED-ULT POINT IS THE ONE I would most want kept: the page tells the player three separate times to sidestep or dodge Pop Blossom's wind-up, and Riot's own passive text says the preparation is hidden while she is disguised. That advice cannot be followed. CHAMPION-WIDE, VERIFIED ON THE WIKI: Void Stone is 10% magic damage reduction, not 15% (V11.24); Force Pulse has not been charge-gated since V12.23 and the phases[2].why boilerplate is wrong on all 71 Kassadin matchups; and the kit file still reproduces Riot's pre-rework tooltip, so both errors will regenerate unless fixed at the source. _missing-interactions.json's entry here ('Neeko can cancel your Null Sphere with Inherent Glamour, Tangle-Barbs, Pop Blossom') is inverted — Null Sphere interrupts channels, it is not one — and was not used.
